featured_reviews.name: Shuvayu Mukherjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Last update 8-Dec-2020: One CCS2 cable is made available for general public. Meaning, good for Nexon EV, Cona and SZ :-) thank you Tata Power!! 👍

All the chargers were working when I visited but there was no one to help. The CCS chaging plug went into the socket of my Nexon EV. The machine has a QR code (see the pic) but there is no mention of which app to use! It says to tap your RFID card. I tried my debit card. The machine did recognise it and the charger got locked into the car socket and the display showed time and KW but both were stuck at zero. The charging never started. I had to push the orange emergency stop button on the left side of the charger to unlock it!

There is no phone number mentioned. No name mentioned of the app to be used of the details of the RFID card. I reached home with 6% SOC with the AC turned off sweating in the humid heat.

UPDATE: I came to know after speaking with Tata Power EV charging specialist that this is their test facility and not available to general public. There is only one charger available for taxis Bharat DC001 (evarito and e2o type socket). CCS2 type (Cona, Nexon or ZS) will not be able to fast charge here.

featured_reviews.name: SGT Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tata Power EV Charging Station – Near LTT (Lokmanya Tilak Terminus)

Finding this charging point is honestly half the battle  charging is the easier part.

This Tata Power charger is located right outside Platform 1 at LTT, towards the far end of the station, close to the Haldiram/Coach Hotel side. Do not expect clear signage. You have to enter through the Pay & Park area, and the only smart move is to tell the parking attendant upfront that you’re here to charge your EV  otherwise you’ll keep circling the station like it’s a maze.

Once you reach it, the setup itself is fairly straightforward.

I’ve been using this charging point for over a year now, multiple times, and based on experience:

It works around 7 out of 10 times

Not perfect, but far more reliable than many city chargers

We’ve mostly used the CCS2 connector, which has been stable in most sessions. Charging speed is decent, and once connected, things usually go smoothly without random disconnects.

This is not a fancy or comfortable charging locationit’s functional, utilitarian, and very “Mumbai station energy.” But when it works, it works and that reliability matters more than aesthetics for an EV owner.

Bottom line:
Hard to reach, average infrastructure, but dependable enough to keep coming back. If you’re near LTT and need a quick top-up, this charger is worth knowing just go in prepared.

Pro tip:
Don’t rely only on maps. Speak to the parking staff immediately it’ll save you time, patience, and battery percentage.

— SGT Reviews | Sip. Grab. Taste. (and Charge

featured_reviews.name: Suffiyan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am writing to raise a serious complaint regarding my worst experience at one of your Ather charging stations. I was unfairly charged for parking, which I believe is not justified because, to my knowledge, wherever an Ather charger is installed, the parking space rent is already paid by Ather. What made the situation worse was the extremely rude and unprofessional behavior of the staff present at the location.
(1) The staff did not inform me in advance that the parking was paid. Only after I connected my charger and waited for nearly 10 minutes was I told that it was a paid parking space. (2) If this information had been shared beforehand, I would have vacated the spot immediately and not connected the charger at all. (3) Since this is an MCGM parking space and Ather is already paying rent for it, I do not understand how customers can be charged again for parking.
